verses.text: Now Joseph had been taken down to Egypt. Potiphar, an Egyptian who was one of Pharaoh's officials and the captain of the guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had taken him there.
The LORD was with Joseph, and everything went well for him. He lived in the house of his Egyptian master.
His master saw that the LORD was with him and that the LORD made everything he did succeed.
Joseph pleased his master and became his personal servant. Potiphar put him in charge of his household, and he trusted him with everything he owned.

From the time Potiphar put him in charge of his household and of everything he owned, the LORD blessed the household of the Egyptian because of Joseph. The LORD's blessing was on everything Potiphar had, both in the house and in the fields.
So Potiphar left everything he had in Joseph's care. With Joseph in charge, he did not worry about anything except the food he ate. Now Joseph was strong and handsome.
After a while, his master's wife noticed Joseph and said, "Come to bed with me!"
But he refused. He said to her, "With me in charge, my master does not worry about anything in the house. He has trusted me with everything he owns.
No one in this house is greater than I am. My master has kept nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. So how could I do such a wicked thing and sin against God?"
She kept on asking Joseph day after day, but he refused to go to bed with her or even be with her.
One day he went into the house to do his work, and none of the household servants were inside.
She grabbed him by his cloak and said, "Come to bed with me!" But he left his cloak in her hand and ran out of the house.
When she saw that he had left his cloak in her hand and had run out of the house,
she called her household servants. "Look," she said to them, "this Hebrew has been brought here to make fools of us! He came in here to sleep with me, but I screamed.
When he heard me scream for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house."
She kept his cloak beside her until his master came home.
Then she told him the same story: "That Hebrew slave you brought us came to me to make a fool of me.
But as soon as I screamed for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house."
When his master heard the story his wife told him, saying, "This is how your slave treated me", he became furious.
Joseph's master took him and put him in prison, the place where the king's prisoners were kept. So Joseph stayed there in prison.
But the LORD was with Joseph and showed him kindness. He made the prison warden like him.
So the warden put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners in the prison, and Joseph was responsible for everything that was done there.
The warden did not need to check on anything that Joseph was in charge of, because the LORD was with Joseph and made everything he did succeed.
